title: Return to stock under 247 CMR 9.13: the container label, the policy and procedure, and the recall bar
subtopic: Return to stock of medication prepared but not dispensed
rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 9.13(1), in the event a pharmacy prepares a prescription for dispensing but the medication is not dispensed, the pharmacy may return the medication to stock, and a pharmacy shall ensure the following conditions are satisfied if it does: it may not return the medication to the manufacturer's stock bottle; and it shall keep the medication in the original patient container or place it in an appropriate container and shall affix a label to the container containing the product name, the strength or concentration, the name of the manufacturer, supplier, or NDC number, and the expiration date assigned at the time of filling. Under 247 CMR 9.13(2) a pharmacy shall maintain a policy and procedure regarding returning medications to stock. Under 247 CMR 9.13(3), in the event of a recall, a pharmacy may not dispense any medication that has been returned to stock and is potentially subject to the recall unless it can confirm the specific lot number is not included in the recall.
exam_relevance: Tests the conditions that attach once a pharmacy chooses to return a prepared but undispensed medication to stock: the stock-bottle bar, the four label elements, the required policy and procedure, and the lot-confirmation condition on dispensing during a recall.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations

exceptions: During a recall, returned-to-stock medication potentially subject to the recall may be dispensed only if the pharmacy can confirm the specific lot number is not included in the recall.
common_confusions: 247 CMR 9.13 states no time limit for returning medication to stock.

The four label elements in 247 CMR 9.13(1)(b) do not include a lot number, but 247 CMR 9.13(3) bars dispensing potentially recalled returned-to-stock medication unless the specific lot number can be confirmed as not included.
Returning medication to stock is permitted, not required, and never into the manufacturer's stock bottle.
verification_notes: Read on 2026-09-16 in the Board of Registration in Pharmacy's publication of 247 CMR 9.00 on mass.gov (PDF, Mass. Register #1536, 12/6/2024).
